did_you_know.text: Did you know? The remnant of Judah was not merely a small group; it included the army commanders, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
Did you know? The people asked Jeremiah to pray for them because only a few of them remained after the disaster that had struck Judah.
Did you know? The people’s request to Jeremiah was twofold: to learn which way they should go and to know what they should do.

Did you know? The people pledged that the word of the LORD would be binding testimony for them, declaring that they would do whatever the LORD commanded, whether they considered the answer good or bad.
Did you know? Jeremiah did not give the LORD’s answer immediately; the word of the LORD came to him only after ten days.
Did you know? The instruction given to the people was to remain in the land. In that context, the LORD promised to build them up and plant them, rather than tear them down and uproot them.
Did you know? Although the people feared the king of Babylon, the message given to them was not to fear him, because the LORD promised to be with them, save them, and deliver them from his power.
Did you know? The warning about Egypt was presented as a condition: if the people refused to remain in the land and would not obey the voice of the LORD, a new danger would overtake them.
Did you know? Jeremiah warned that the sword and famine the people feared would not disappear in Egypt; instead, they would catch up with them and cling to them there.

Did you know? At the end of his message, Jeremiah said that the people had asked him to inquire of the LORD but had not kept their promise to obey him. Therefore, he again warned them of death by sword, famine, and plague in Egypt.
